title: Portugal Surprisingly Hand Ronaldo’s No. 7 Jersey to Premier League Flop
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom7:41 AM ESTCristiano Ronaldo’s No. 7 shirt will be a heavy one to wear. / Ryan Pierse/FIFA/Getty ImagesCarlos Forbs may not have been able to break through at Wolverhampton Wanderers, but the jet-heeled 22-year-old winger has been entrusted as Portugal’s first No.7 since Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement from international soccer.

There has been much speculation about who will take on the burden of a digit which has become indelibly linked to one player for the past two decades since Portugal can’t retire the number due to FIFA’s strict numerical regulations.

While Lionel Scaloni was able to name an Argentina roster without a new No. 10 in Lionel Messi’s first absence given the friendly nature of Friday’s fixture with Uruguay, the rules of the Nations League have forced Jorge Jesus’s hand ahead of Saturday’s clash with Denmark.

The veteran coach who played a significant role in Ronaldo’s abrupt retirement has now shifted the spotlight onto the unlikely figure of Forbs, who will wear the No. 7 for at least this month, as revealed by Portugal’s official squad list on UEFA’s website.

For those whose only exposure to the pint-sized speedster was his underwhelming loan spell at Wolves during a 2024–25 season spent flirting with relegation, this honor may come as a surprise. Yet, the Club Brugge forward could come to represent an inspired choice.

Forbs will get a new-look No. 7 jersey. Rather than the familiar digit design, Portugal’s No. 7 will now forever contain a slash through the middle of it, to offer a clear delineation in time before and after Ronaldo.

“This is yet another way to immortalize the significance of such a special number and to honor the legacy it represents,” a gushing statement from the Portuguese soccer federation read. “Because there are stories, memories, achievements, and emotions that will forever be linked to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“From today [Nov. 14] on, the No. 7 on the jersey will look different, yet it will carry the same essence and the same pride—while the previous design is set aside to immortalize a story that will never be forgotten.

Carlos Forbs is having an excellent season. / Gregory Van Gansen/Photonews/Getty ImagesAge: 22Club: Club BruggePortugal caps: 1Portugal goals: 0The signs that Forbs would take on the No. 7 had always been there. Galatasaray’s mercurial winger Rafael Leão had been given the digit when Ronaldo sulked out of Portugal’s September-October camp but missed out on November’s roster due to a muscular injury.

The likes of João Félix, Pedro Neto, Francisco Trincão or Geovany Quenda could all have feasibly assumed the mantle. Roma’s teenage prodigy Rodrigo Mora publicly distanced himself from the shirt this month. “No, no, no, I don’t think about that, it is far too much for me,” he warned with a smile. However, when Ronaldo was last absent for Portugal, it was Forbs who took on the challenge.

After getting duped into needless red card against the Republic of Ireland a year ago, Ronaldo’s No. 7 shirt was worn by Forbs. The winger came off the bench to win a penalty in Portugal’s 9–1 annihilation of Armenia.

That stood alone as Forbs’s only senior international cap heading into the November break. The Club Brugge forward missed out on the World Cup roster and was overlooked for the fall fixtures, but Jesus couldn’t turn him down for much longer.

Carlos Forbs never quite made it at Wolverhampton Wanderers. / Malcolm Couzens/Getty ImagesForbs has always been seen as a figure with immense potential. The electric left footer joined Manchester City’s academy as a 10-year-old and would blossom into one of the club’s most exciting prospects, earning recognition as the Premier League 2 Player of the Season in 2022–23. That summer Ajax spent €14 million ($15.4 million) on a teenager without a single senior appearance to his name.
A difficult debut season at an Ajax side which churned through four managers in three months convinced Forbs to return to England with a loan spell at Wolves. It never clicked.

“To do what I want in this system is difficult for him when we are defending,” Wolves’ Portuguese coach Vítor Pereira explained, pointing out how his preferred back-three formation left little room for a classical winger like Forbs. “He doesn’t have the skill to go and come back to defend, it’s difficult.

“It’s not about his quality because he has quality, he’s strong one against one, he’s very fast. But in my system, he cannot play inside in between the lines because he doesn’t have these skills. And to play outside is a different profile of player.”
Despite remaining fit for most of the campaign, Forbs was given only one Premier League start all season and featured just twice after the turn of the year.
Upon his return to the Netherlands, Ajax cut their losses on Forbs and offloaded him to Club Brugge in 2025, where he would rediscover the potential that had always been bubbling beneath the surface.
